title: Google DeepMind Computes Electronic Quantum Excited States with Parameter-Free Neural Wavefunctions
whyItMatters: Published in Science: transforms excited-state quantum mechanics into a parameter-free expanded ground-state problem for FermiNet/Psiformer, cracking hard double excitations and optical spectra at chemical accuracy.
summary: Google DeepMind researchers David Pfau, Simon Axelrod, Halvard Sutterud, Ingrid von Glehn, and James S. Spencer (with Imperial College London, Harvard, and MIT) published Natural Excited States (NES-VMC) in Science, solving a decades-old obstacle in quantum Monte Carlo: computing electronic excited states without arbitrary penalty hyperparameters or explicit orthogonalization. By reformulating the search for the lowest K excited states as finding the ground state of an expanded multi-state system and pairing it with FermiNet and Psiformer neural wavefunctions, the method accurately predicts excitation energies, transition dipole moments, oscillator strengths, and notoriously difficult double excitations on benzene-scale molecules.
technicalHighlights: Introduces a parameter-free variational Monte Carlo formulation (NES-VMC) requiring no state orthogonalization or penalty tuning.
Computes arbitrary quantum observables including off-diagonal transition dipole moments and oscillator strengths governing light absorption and emission.
Paired with FermiNet and Psiformer, achieves chemical accuracy on benzene-scale vertical excitations and challenging double-excitation states.
caveats: Variational Monte Carlo with deep neural wavefunctions remains computationally intensive for very large macromolecules compared to TD-DFT, though vastly more accurate on correlated excited states.

scoreRationale.foundational: Extends ab initio deep neural wavefunctions from ground states to the full excited-state spectrum governing photochemistry, solar harvesting, and vision.
scoreRationale.ripple: Impacts computational chemistry, photocatalysis, OLEDs, atomic/nuclear physics, and correlated condensed-matter physics.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Science (Aug 2024) with rigorous ab initio benchmarks against experimental spectra and coupled-cluster references.
scoreRationale.velocity: Eliminates brittle penalty tuning and enables accurate neural computation of double excitations that defeat standard quantum chemistry.
